Domestic hindrances
On the purely practical side the shortage of domestic help is one of the biggest hind- rances to women who want to go out to work. It is true that electricity with the use of labour-saving equipment which it has made possible has been one of the biggest eman- cipators of women, but even the robot maid- servants of the future forecast by Professor Thring and the Postmaster-General will not look after the children when mother is out. Here there is a crying need for more properly supervised play groups and day nurseries, the case for which has been most eloquently put in a recently published report on the Care of Pre-School Children by Simon Yudkin.† Then there is the problem of family illness.
